data_class.diffeo_quotient: genericity is defined on data modulo diffeomorphisms that are asymptotically the identity; constructing that quotient rigorously is a declared open technical gap (see unresolved_items), not a solved step
data_class.excluded_data: data outside the declared generic set are non-generic; they are NOT counterexamples to this class. The schema does NOT decide individual membership (see genericity.membership_ruling), and the meagerness of the named families is unresolved - so 'outside G' may not be asserted for a named datum without a proof. [R1 minor: this field previously conflicted with membership_ruling and with falsifier.schema_falsifiers.]
data_class.gauge: no gauge is fixed on the data; every predicate in this schema is diffeomorphism invariant

regularity_class.default: smooth-with-decay: h and K of class C^infinity with the numeric rates below

genericity.acceptance_alignment: Astra F1 acceptance names 'open dense'. This schema's frozen default is the residual/comeager form; open_dense_escape is registered below as a distinct STRICTLY STRONGER variant (a dense open set is comeager, so it implies the default) and is never silently substituted. A gate matching only the literal words 'open dense' would accept a stronger class than this one - recorded as a vocabulary risk.
genericity.ambient_space: the constraint manifold X^r_vac(AF) of one-ended asymptotically flat VACUUM initial data in the declared regularity class, carrying the topology induced from the weighted Sobolev product H^s_delta x H^{s-1}_{delta+1}. R1 F04 accepted: the topology is the SUBSPACE topology on the constraint set, not the topology of the unconstrained product (under the latter reading X_vac itself is meager and no G exists). X_vac is a closed subset of a Banach space, hence a Baire space, so comeagerness is non-vacuous and G is non-empty.
genericity.class_change_warning: genericity is part of the class identity. The comeager form is this class. 'For all data' is strictly stronger. The dense-open form is ALSO strictly stronger, because a dense open set is comeager (it is the countable intersection of the constant family). The comeager form does not imply the dense-open form (a comeager set can have empty interior). No strengthening may be substituted silently. See genericity.transfer_failures for the two directions.
genericity.excluded_set: the excluded set is REQUIRED to be meager; whether the named candidate families are meager is UNRESOLVED, so they are listed as obligations rather than as constructions. Candidates: data with a nonzero Killing field, data in the exactly-extendible (Cauchy-horizon) family, self-similar or scale-invariant data, finite-dimensional analytic families generated by continuation, and exactly symmetric data (see axis_registry and membership_ruling).
genericity.generic_set: G = intersection over n >= 1 of U_n with each U_n open and dense in X^r_vac(AF); equivalently the complement is meager (first category); G_r is non-empty because X_vac is Baire
genericity.membership_ruling: set-level only: the class quantifies over a comeager set G of data; the schema does not decide membership of an individual datum. A single symmetric/stationary datum is expected outside G in the vacuum class, but that expectation is a proof obligation, not a schema field (flash-04 AMB-07 ruling).
genericity.topology_or_measure: subspace topology induced on X^r_vac(AF); Frechet topology for the smooth-with-decay class. Gauge invariance is handled by noting every predicate here is diffeomorphism invariant; the quotient by asymptotically-identity diffeomorphisms is NOT used to define comeagerness and remains an open technical gap (see unresolved_items).

transfer_failures.witness: let C = intersection over n of U_n with each U_n open dense and of measure < 1/n; C is comeager and Lebesgue-null, so comeagerness does not yield full measure (a single fat-Cantor complement is open dense but not null, which is why the countable intersection is used) [R1 F03]

let C be the comeager null set of the row above; then X minus C is meager and has full measure, so full measure does not yield comeagerness. (The irrationals are BOTH comeager and full-measure and therefore witness nothing - R1 F03.)
the irrationals are comeager with empty interior: a comeager set need not contain any nonempty open subset, so the comeager form does not yield a dense-open form
a fat Cantor set is nowhere dense (meager) yet has positive measure, so it is not contained in any countable union of finite-codimension submanifolds, which is null

transfer_holds.witness: a dense open set U is the countable intersection of the constant family {U}, hence comeager; the dense-open form implies the comeager form
a proper closed finite-codimension submanifold is closed and nowhere dense, so a countable union of them is meager; if the exceptional set is so covered, the property holds on a comeager set

variants.relation: implied by residual_comeager in a Baire space (a comeager set is dense); a dense set need not be comeager, so it is strictly weaker than the class default. [R2-16 corrected: was off-vocabulary and mislabelled incomparable]

variants.requires: a specified measure on X, e.g. a Gaussian measure induced by the constraint map

i_plus.completeness_definition: every null geodesic generator of I+ is future-complete: it is defined for all values of the affine parameter induced by gtilde; equivalently every future-directed null geodesic reaching I+ has infinite affine length with respect to g
i_plus.completeness_definition_status: definitional restatement of generator completeness. It is NOT the unverified equivalence recorded in conclusion.equivalent_standard_formulation, and it asserts no theorem (worker-16 F1-16-01 clarification).
i_plus.completion_uniqueness: NOT asserted: the schema requires existence of a conformal completion of the stated regularity. Uniqueness up to conformal isometry fixing I+ is not claimed. [R1 minor]
i_plus.definition: conformal completion of (M,g) at future null infinity: an embedding into (Mtilde,gtilde) with Omega > 0 on M, Omega = 0 and dOmega != 0 on I+, gtilde = Omega^2 g of class C^k Lorentzian on Mtilde = M union I+, I+ a null hypersurface diffeomorphic to R x S^2, with the conformal Einstein equations holding near I+ to the order required by k
forbidden_weakenings: replacing completeness by mere existence of I+
assuming I+ complete rather than concluding it
assuming asymptotic simplicity or that I+ is the entire conformal boundary
i_plus.k_is_a_class_parameter: the exponent k in 'C^k completion' is part of the class assumption (i_plus_regularity), not a physical conclusion; statement_formal concludes existence of a completion OF THAT ASSUMED REGULARITY. [R1 minor]
i_plus.predicate_abbreviation: AF_{I+}(M) abbreviates the existence predicate of i_plus.definition: M admits a conformal completion (Mtilde,gtilde,Omega) at future null infinity with the regularity assumed in i_plus_regularity. It introduces no assumption beyond that leaf and is the only reading of the symbol in this schema. [rev12: F1-review-090 HF and F1-review-19 HF-06 - the symbol was previously undefined; grep AF_{I+} matched conclusion.statement_formal only]
required_properties: I+ non-empty, null, and diffeomorphic to R x S^2
I+ future-complete in the affine parameter of gtilde
no generator of I+ terminates at a singular point of the conformal boundary

non_vacuity.condition: G must contain data whose MGHD is future geodesically incomplete; otherwise the 'no visible singularity' clause has no content and the class is trivially satisfied by dispersion. The stronger requirement that the black-hole region B be non-empty belongs to the separate black-hole-formation statement and is NOT assumed here (worker-16 F1-16-03 accepted).
non_vacuity.status: trapped-surface formation is standard, but membership of such a family in the comeager set is exactly what must be supplied; UNVERIFIED here
non_vacuity.vacuity_falsifier: if every data set admitted by the schema disperses to a future-complete development, the schema is vacuous and must be revised rather than cited
non_vacuity.witness_type: a one-parameter family in G containing a future trapped surface (sufficiently concentrated AF vacuum data), hence a future-incomplete development

D0.definition: admissible regularity indices, a tagged disjoint union: r = smooth (the smooth-with-decay default) or r = (sobolev,s,delta) with s > 5/2 and delta in (1/2,1). X^r_vac(AF) is the corresponding one-ended AF vacuum constraint manifold (Frechet for r = smooth; weighted Sobolev product H^s_delta x H^{s-1}_{delta+1} for r = (sobolev,s,delta)). The index r ranges over exactly D0, so the smooth branch is no longer typed as a pair and the class does not range over 'suitable' regularity. [rev12 F-2 well-typedness repair: F1-review-19 F-2, F2b-review-034 HF-034-1]

D1.definition: comeager (residual) subsets of X^r_vac(AF): G_r = intersection over n >= 1 of U_n with each U_n open and dense in the named topology; equivalently X^r_vac(AF) minus G_r is meager

D2.definition: one-ended asymptotically flat vacuum initial data satisfying both constraint equations in the declared regularity class

D3.definition: conformal completions of the maximal development at future null infinity: Omega > 0 on M, Omega = 0 and dOmega != 0 on I+, gtilde = Omega^2 g extends as a C^k Lorentzian metric to M union I+, I+ null and diffeomorphic to R x S^2

D4.definition: future-directed causal geodesics gamma: [0,T) -> M that are future-inextendible in M, with T < infinity in affine parameter (unit speed in the timelike case). Qualifier aligned with visibility.definition and non_vacuity: future-inextendibility is what makes the terminal end a singularity. [R1 minor]

D5.definition: pairs (q,t0) with q a point of I+ and t0 in [0,T) such that the tail gamma([t0,T)) is contained in the causal past J^-(q) intersected with M. Whole-curve containment gamma([0,T)) subset J^-(q) is strictly STRONGER and is NOT the predicate of this class [rev12: F1-review-19 HF-06 critical, independently confirmed by worker-037 W037V2-F1 and worker-078 W078-F1-QUANT-ADJ-01]

quantifiers.formal: forall r in D0: exists G_r subset X^r_vac(AF) with G_r comeager: forall (Sigma,h,K) in G_r, letting (M,g) be the maximal globally hyperbolic development: exists a conformal completion (Mtilde,gtilde,Omega) of (M,g) at I+ such that (i) I+ is null with I+ diffeomorphic to R x S^2, and (ii) every null geodesic generator of I+ is future-complete, and forall future-inextendible causal geodesics gamma of (M,g) with finite affine length: not exists q in I+ and t0 in [0,T) with gamma([t0,T)) subset J^-(q) intersect M.
quantifiers.negation: there exists r in D0 such that for every comeager G_r subset X^r_vac(AF) there is (Sigma,h,K) in G_r whose development fails the conclusion: either it admits no conformal completion of the declared kind, or some null geodesic generator of I+ is incomplete, or some future-inextendible causal geodesic of finite affine length has a tail visible from I+.
quantifiers.negation_normal_form: { r in D0 : { D in X^r_vac(AF) : not P_WCC(D) } is non-meager } is non-empty
quantifiers.order_note: the generic set is chosen before and independently of the data; it may not depend on (Sigma,h,K). Swapping the first exists and the following forall yields the trivial statement that every data set lies in some comeager set.
quantifiers.quantifier_class: forall-exists(comeager)-forall-exists-forall-not-exists; not reducible to a first-order statement over the data because the comeager set is a set quantifier

tier_1.genericity_requirement: tier 1 refutes the class by showing the not-P set is NON-MEAGER in the ambient space (equivalently: it meets every comeager set). Exhibiting a single datum with not-P is NOT sufficient in general: G is existentially quantified and the schema's membership_ruling leaves individual membership undecided, so the datum may lie outside every admissible witness G. If the class is INSTANTIATED with a concrete, explicitly constructed generic set G*, then one datum in G* with not-P refutes the instantiated statement - a different, hypothesis-stronger claim. Route R1 = non-meagerness (general refutation); route R2 = a datum in an instantiated G* (instantiated claims only). [R1 F01 accepted; the earlier text wrongly made R1 a general route]

The class asserts hiddenness of singularities, not their absence.

visibility.definition: a future-inextendible causal geodesic gamma: [0,T) -> M with T < infinity in affine parameter is visible from I+ iff there exists q in I+ AND t0 in [0,T) such that the TAIL gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q) intersect M. Visibility is a property of the singular END of the geodesic, so the tail formulation is used; requiring the whole geodesic to lie in J^-(q) would misclassify a geodesic that starts in the exterior and ends inside the black-hole region. [R1 F02 accepted]
must_not_conflate: bounded affine length is the notion used, not curvature-scalar blow-up; a curvature singularity inside a horizon is not a counterexample
visibility is via a causal relation to a point of I+, not via a geodesic that merely escapes to spatial infinity i0
a singularity hidden inside B is consistent with this class and is not a failure
single-q non-containment (the formal negation) must not be replaced by B-containment; see negation_conclusion [R1 F02]
visibility.negation_conclusion: there is NO visible_singularity_from_I_plus: for every future-inextendible causal geodesic gamma of finite affine length, for every q in I+ and every t0 in [0,T), the tail gamma([t0,T)) is NOT contained in J^-(q) intersect M - no single point of I+ causally precedes the singular end of gamma. This is NOT equivalent to 'gamma is contained in B = M minus J^-(I+)': B-containment is strictly stronger, and a geodesic may begin in J^-(I+) and end in the black-hole region. [R1 F02 accepted; the earlier 'i.e. inside B' equivalence was false]
visibility.observability_note: the class is falsifiable in principle by one visible singularity only if the failure set is shown non-meager; see falsifier.tier_1 vs tier_2
visibility.singularity_definition: an incomplete causal geodesic: future-directed, future-inextendible in M, with finite affine length (unit speed in the timelike case). Curvature blow-up is NOT used as the definition of a singular point.
visibility.visible_singularity_exists: exists gamma visible from I+ in the sense above
visibility.witness_protocol: for a claimed counterexample: (1) constraint residuals below tolerance; (2) AF decay rates at the declared orders; (3) gamma future-inextendible with finite affine parameter; (4) causal relation gamma subset J^-(q) for an exhibited q in I+. Step (5), genericity membership or non-meagerness of the failure set, is NOT machine-checkable and must be argued separately.

genericity.class_change_warning: genericity is part of the class identity. The comeager form is this class. 'For all data' is strictly stronger. The dense-open form is ALSO strictly stronger, because a dense open set is comeager (it is the countable intersection of the constant family). The comeager form does not imply the dense-open form (a comeager set can have empty interior). No strengthening may be substituted silently.
genericity.excluded_set: meager; must contain (status unresolved) the stationary/axisymmetric Kerr data, whose maximal development DOES admit a C-infinity vacuum extension, plus self-similar and finite-dimensional analytic families
genericity.generic_set: G = countable intersection of open dense subsets of X^r_vac(AF); complement meager; non-empty by Baire-ness
genericity.topology_or_measure: subspace topology on the constraint manifold; Frechet topology for the smooth-with-decay class. The diffeomorphism quotient is not used to define comeagerness (open technical gap).

a fat Cantor set is meager with positive measure, hence not covered by countably many finite-codimension submanifolds

transfer_holds.witness: a dense open set U is the countable intersection of the constant family {U}, hence comeager; the dense-open form implies the comeager form

non_vacuity.c2_specific_note: the vacuity argument (a future geodesically complete development admits no proper future extension) is ASSERTED here as a proof obligation, NOT as an established fact. The one-line reason (a maximal geodesic of the complete development cannot terminate at a boundary point of the extension) needs a Lorentzian-distance / causality step in M-prime, and M-prime is NOT assumed globally hyperbolic, so the step is not free. No counterexample is known in the frozen AF Lambda=0 class; the claim is marked UNVERIFIED pending a derivation or an L1 source. [R2 major accepted]
non_vacuity.condition: the class must be applied to data whose maximal development is not future geodesically complete. The expectation that a future-complete development admits no proper future extension is a proof obligation, NOT an elementary fact (see c2_specific_note); if it fails, the class would be vacuous on complete developments and must be revised rather than cited.

non_vacuity.witness_type: one-parameter family in G whose development contains a future trapped surface, hence is future geodesically incomplete

D0.definition: admissible regularity indices, a tagged disjoint union: r = smooth (the smooth-with-decay default) or r = (sobolev,s,delta) with s > 5/2 and delta in (1/2,1). X^r_vac(AF) is the corresponding one-ended AF vacuum constraint manifold (Frechet for r = smooth; weighted Sobolev product H^s_delta x H^{s-1}_{delta+1} for r = (sobolev,s,delta)). The index r ranges over exactly D0, so the smooth branch is no longer typed as a pair and the class does not range over 'suitable' regularity. [rev12 F-2 well-typedness repair: F1-review-19 F-2, F2b-review-034 HF-034-1]

quantifiers.formal: forall r in D0: exists G_r subset X^r_vac(AF) with G_r comeager: forall (Sigma,h,K) in G_r, letting (M,g) be the maximal globally hyperbolic development: not exists a proper future C2 vacuum extension (M',g',iota) of (M,g).

_prose.promotion_rule: may be recorded as a theorem only with a checked proof artifact and artifact_refs; a schema is never evidence for its own conclusion
_prose.scope_statement: The maximal globally hyperbolic development of generic asymptotically flat vacuum initial data (4-dimensional Einstein vacuum equations, Lambda = 0) admits no proper future extension whose metric is merely continuous (C0) and Lorentzian; no differentiability, no curvature, and no equation requirement are assumed of the extension. The class is about non-extendibility of the development; it makes no statement about what an observer at I+ sees.
unresolved_items: the correct definition of 'extension' for merely continuous metrics (geodesic uniqueness may fail)

visibility.derived_note: inextendibility is a statement about the boundary of the development, not about causal relations to I+
visibility.forbidden_falsifier: a visible incomplete causal geodesic is a WCC falsifier; it is NOT the falsifier of this class
visibility.reason: visibility from I+ is the WCC predicate. This SCC class asserts non-extendibility of the maximal development; a singularity can be invisible from I+ and still the development can be extendible, and vice versa. The two axes are logically independent as stated.
